correctness.rationale: The theorem follows from three independently inspectable ingredients: (i) an exact atomic-extension first-order type recursion valid for every finite graph, (ii) a direct proof that paths of order at least seven share a three-round type and that Cartesian products preserve three-round equivalence, and (iii) exhaustive enumeration of the 28 path-product canonical graphs. The attached code constructs all adjacencies and type signatures and plays the direct three-round EF game for all 66 pairs of distinct representatives. The sharp representative bound equals the largest class-minimum graph order, ten. Computed finite claims are verified at their supplied actual package paths, not extrapolated to infinity.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The result is not a corollary of product preservation alone, because converse preservation is false: the factors of 2-by-5 and 3-by-4 have different depth-three path types yet their Cartesian products share one depth-three graph type. A finite exact census, with independent adversarial-game comparisons for distinct classes, supplies the missing implication.

originality.rationale: Accessible primary comparisons do not state or imply the full twelve-class rank-three classification of undirected rectangular grid graphs. Brown–Hoshino classify paths and cycles separately; a known Cartesian-product game congruence yields a finite reduction but not a converse or the exact cross-dimensional collapse; Kopczyński studies axiomatization in a different, richer signature. Targeted scientific-index and bibliographic searches did not locate a covering classification. This is a best-knowledge assessment, not a proof of absolute novelty.
residual_risks: Unindexed older mathematical-logic literature or unpublished notes could have an equivalent exact rank-three grid classification.
General finite-model-theory literature may package the same twenty-eight-case census under a different vocabulary; no general absence can be certified from indexed searches.

value.rationale: Complete classification of a classical natural graph family in pure first-order adjacency logic, with a sharp optimal test-set size, is a precise reusable finite-model-theory invariant. Factorwise stabilization gives only a loose 28-case canonical bound; the exact 12-case collapse and 2-by-5 versus 3-by-4 equivalence reveal unexpected loss of shape at low logical depth. The classification lets every depth-three graph sentence on any finite rectangular grid be tested on twelve small representatives. The exact invariant and its optimal bound, not an arbitrary numerical slice, motivate the finite computation.
